chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
title: The overloaded excursion boat in Washington with Sarah and Dinah Washington
summary: Too many tickets were sold, people crowd on, the boat sinks lower and the musicians jump to the dock.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: It was a very enjoyable situation working with both of these fellows. We had some nice times, some funny times. I remember one time we were booked to play a boat in Washington with Sarah Vaughan and her trio, and Dinah Washington and her trio, and someone else. And the crowd was so big, the people that booked the thing had not given out tickets in proportion to the capacity of the boat. What happened was that when people came down to get on the boat, the boat was full, it was loaded, and there were still about as many people standing out on the dock to get on the boat as there were people on the boat! These people were being held back, and they were pretty mad about the whole situation, so they began to climb on the boat. So everybody was looking over the side, we were looking over the side, and the water was coming up and the boat was going down. So we said to ourselves, it's best to get off while we can get off, and some of the guys were jumping off the boat onto the dock... Somehow we happened to get off. And the captain just had to bring up the gangplank and go down the river a ways to ease the tension. Nevertheless, at that particular time, we jumped off the boat, so I didn't ever know what happened.
But it was just one of those times that it was a funny situation. When you're on the road and things like that happen, it goes to make for happy times that you remember.
